chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abd al-Karim, from Yazid ibn Khalifa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: There was a basket in my house containing eggs from the pigeons of the Sanctuary (Haram). My servant went and overturned the basket, not knowing there were eggs in it, and broke them. I went out and met Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan, and I mentioned that to him. He said: 'Give charity with two handfuls of fine flour.' He said: Then I met Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and informed him. He said: 'The price of two birds, which you feed to the pigeons of the Sanctuary.' I met Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan after that and informed him, and he said: 'He is truthful, so take his ruling, for he took it from his fathers (peace be upon them).'

key_terms.صَدَقَ: He is truthful/correct (used to confirm a ruling)
key_terms.مِكْتَلٌ: A basket or container for holding grain or eggs

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for accidentally breaking sanctuary pigeons' eggs?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific expiation for accidentally breaking sanctuary pigeons' eggs, prescribing the feeding of the birds with flour valued at two birds. The narrative highlights the scholarly validation of this ruling by Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan, who confirmed its authenticity by tracing it back to the Imams' ancestors, thereby establishing a consistent juristic precedent for accidental damages within the Haram.
